title: [readability] PeerHealthState::select_peer() round-robin logic is underdocumented
description:
The round-robin peer selection algorithm in relay_health.rs (lines 87-118) works correctly but the logic is subtle and poorly documented:

Lines 110-115 find the first eligible peer index >= rr_index, then wrap to position 0 in the *eligible* list if none qualify. The next rr_index is then set to (chosen_idx + 1) % n, where rr_index is tracked in the full peer list space, not the eligible list space.

This design ensures that even if a peer is repeatedly flapping up/down, the next selection will advance through the full list, not just the eligible subset. However:

1. Why is rr_index stored as a position in the full peer list rather than relative to the eligible list?
2. Why does unwrap_or(0) wrap to position 0 of the *eligible* list instead of wrapping rr_index?

This confusion will cause a future maintainer to either misunderstand the behavior or introduce bugs during refactoring. The docstring at line 79-86 describes the eligibility criteria but not the selection order or how wrapping works.

Recommendation: Add a detailed comment block explaining the round-robin design (e.g., why rr_index is in peer list space, what wrapping behavior ensures).
